title: Boosted ART and midazolam

cues.phrase: the capnography trace becomes infrequent and chest movements become shallower
cues.why: Overt respiratory deterioration makes repeating the sedative unattractive even through ordinary safety reasoning; half the options fall without identifying the booster interaction.

fairness: Pausing sedation and supporting ventilation is a defensible immediate response; unchanged saturation on supplemental oxygen is a valid observation and should remain.

title: Dynamic ultrasound after an equivocal inguinal-hernia examination

cues.phrase: a separate surface swelling that is absent on waking
cues.why: The time/posture pattern favors the uniquely 'Standing' label. This is a weak positional hint, not a complete nonmedical distinction from dynamic MRI.

fairness: Dynamic ultrasound is a defensible initial study for the intermittent groin contour change despite musculoskeletal findings. Dynamic MRI is a plausible alternative, particularly at a different workup stage; no unequivocal clinical error identified.
The stem explicitly establishes no prior imaging. This asks familiar initial-test selection, not two-step reasoning, and is too easy for typical PGY-2/3 residents.
REJECT_BASIC: preserving the initial-test objective does not supply an onboarding purpose. Four nearly identical first-test items should not consume the difficulty exception.
suggestions: Use a technically specified prior examination, such as a negative supine scan performed without provocation, and require choosing an adequate repeat dynamic study versus MRI after an adequate negative study. Supply actual protocol and symptom observations, not the word 'inconclusive'.
Make siblings differ in imaging adequacy or symptom/imaging concordance rather than occupation, age or exertion trigger; re-version the objective if needed.

title: Elective planning for symptomatic inguinal hernia

cues.phrase: Pain at this site repeatedly interrupts the patient's usual activity.
cues.why: This states the standard symptom-burden rationale for elective consultation immediately before the choice. It largely resolves the competing watchful-waiting option; it is necessary decision information, so the repair is a harder decision, not deletion of the symptom burden.

fairness: The ultrasound supports a reducible inguinal hernia, and consultation is reasonable when symptoms limit activity. Coexisting musculoskeletal pain is not thereby disproved; consultation should not promise all pain will resolve after repair.
The already established diagnosis plus a classic symptom threshold yields one familiar management rule, not a demanding two-step task.
REJECT_BASIC: the justification identifies a narrow objective but no actual tutorial function; all four companions repeat the same update and answer.
suggestions: Create a symptom-attribution application: give precise locations and triggers for the patient's limiting pain and observed bulge, including concordant or discordant reproduction during ultrasound/examination. Ask for the next management discussion among repair assessment, targeted musculoskeletal evaluation and observation.
Supply patient goals and operative-risk facts only if they change the decision; use them to support competing plans rather than simply announce a desire for repair.

title: Complete diagnostic biopsy of a suspicious pigmented lesion

cues.phrase: the surrounding lax skin can be brought together around the entire lesion without tension
cues.why: This is effectively permission for the key's 'Entire-lesion excision', and repeats 'entire lesion'. A nonmedical reader can match whole-lesion closure feasibility to the one whole-lesion option.

cues.phrase: Entire-lesion excision with narrow margin into subcutaneous fat
cues.why: The key uniquely specifies a margin and changes sampling category; the other two are near-duplicate punch plans differing only in focus. This isolates the comprehensive option.

fairness: Complete appropriately deep diagnostic sampling is defensible when the whole lesion can be removed safely; the feasibility information is clinically relevant and cannot simply be deleted while retaining competing techniques.
The two punch options are weakly separated; selecting a complete specimen is familiar recognition, too easy for routine resident assessment.
REJECT_BASIC: four copies of the same complete-biopsy rule do not have four distinct introductory roles. The justification does not establish why this is needed in onboarding.
suggestions: Use an actual incomplete specimen whose deep edge, residual raised component and pathology prevent reliable microstaging; ask which targeted completion strategy resolves the uncertainty before definitive staging.

Alternatively use a genuinely constrained site with explicit lesion dimensions and closure limits, then offer clinically defensible sampling approaches. Obtain clinician-supported technique criteria; do not make a correct complete excision wrong by hidden constraints.

title: Interpret a p-value

title: Act and iterate after a PDSA test

cues.phrase: Medication-list entry: total minutes
cues.why: The sole workload increase is in this row (10 to 50), and only the key changes medication-field entry. Simple table matching identifies the answer without clinical or QI knowledge.

cues.phrase: Prefill medication fields; retain escalation prompts
cues.why: Only the key acts on the conspicuous outlier; both alternatives change escalation despite unchanged escalation time and perfect recorded agreement.

cues.phrase: they do not establish a causal treatment effect
cues.why: This pre-answer methods teaching is unnecessary to choose among the three process modifications. It should be in feedback unless causal interpretation is actually tested.

fairness: Testing prefill is a reasonable hypothesis for the observed workload issue; accuracy of manually entered data does not establish accuracy of a proposed prefill source.
The key proposes another small test, so the absence of demonstrated prefill benefit is not itself a fatal fairness flaw. However, availability and provenance of a prefill source are not given.
Too easy for residents: spotting one increased table cell and matching a label is not a meaningful two-step QI decision.

Move the causal-effect teaching sentence to feedback unless it is the object of the question.

title: Tissue confirmation of inflammatory breast cancer

cues.phrase: no tissue block is available
cues.why: Announces the need for tissue architecture after an atypical aspirate, making a core-type approach an obvious upgrade. This is legitimate specimen information, but the standard sampling rule remains simple.

cues.phrase: External systemic staging is planned if invasive carcinoma is confirmed.
cues.why: Previews the purpose of the next tissue step without changing the choice among the three sampling techniques; it is an unnecessary sequencing hint.

fairness: Core sampling of the parenchymal target is a defensible next step for establishing invasive carcinoma and obtaining tissue for characterization. Skin sampling can be complementary but should not be taught as an interchangeable substitute or as never indicated.
The stem supplies a target accessible to ultrasound, an inadequate aspirate and classic inflammatory features. The open-incision competitor is weak for routine initial sampling.

REJECT_BASIC: preserving a harder management companion does not establish a need for this easy introductory rule. The narrow tissue-confirmation objective should not excuse the resident difficulty gap.
suggestions: Develop a documented imaging-pathology discordance after a specific biopsy, then require selecting the next specimen/site or review step. Supply targeting, adequacy and morphology rather than an 'inconclusive' summary.
Keep any essential raw evidence of specimen limitation, but remove the future staging sentence if it has no independent task function.

title: Neoadjuvant sequence for stage III inflammatory breast cancer
fairness: The resident must recognize the initial inflammatory presentation, then resist de-escalating local treatment solely because systemic therapy removes visible and palpable abnormalities.

The key is defensible for the stated nonmetastatic inflammatory phenotype. Exact sequencing and patient eligibility require clinician approval; the item does not specify a drug regimen or imply every skin-redness presentation is inflammatory cancer.
suggestions: Preserve the original extent/time course and conditional response. Do not replace the initial presentation with a diagnosis label that supplies the first inference.

title: Interpret a confidence interval
fairness: The learner must translate the whole relative-risk interval using the fixed control risk, then compare its upper absolute-risk difference with the hypothetical harm margin.

The transformed interval is (0.40-1)*20=-12 to (1.20-1)*20=+4 percentage points; +5 lies outside. The first distractor retains the same conclusion with a wrong interval, so shortcutting directly to the conclusion does not identify the key.
Fixed reference-risk wording avoids an unaddressed second estimated quantity. The conclusion is about this reported interval, not certainty that the true risk cannot exceed the margin.
suggestions: Retain the fixed-risk caveat and parallel numerical alternatives. Feedback should distinguish an interval-model conclusion from proof of no harm.

title: Interpret a p-value
fairness: The resident must separate strong evidence against zero effect from an interval whose entire magnitude falls short of the protocol's target. This tests the common significance-equals-importance error.

The key is correct under the explicit constructed criteria: the null is rejected, and a one-percentage-point reduction is outside the reported interval. It does not establish a clinical threshold for real thyroid surgery.

The criteria are necessary context for a hypothetical protocol, not an automatic cue violation. All four options are balanced; this is moderate at most and less demanding after the parallel statistics siblings.
suggestions: Keep the effect-size conflict and explicit fictional-protocol status. Avoid near-consecutive repeated exposure to B27/B39 as though it measures independent hard reasoning.

title: High-risk peptic-ulcer stigmata requiring endoscopic hemostasis
fairness: The nonbleeding visible vessel warrants a treatment decision despite the dry field. The clip-plus-acid-suppression key is defensible among the offered modalities; the item does not provide a reason to rank it above every other accepted definitive modality.

The task tests a familiar visible-vessel/definitive-modality rule. No major nonmedical option-style cue is apparent, but the injection and powder competitors are easy for residents familiar with this rule.

REJECT_BASIC: explaining why several definitive therapies should not be placed in one ambiguous option set does not establish an onboarding purpose. A rare safety exception is already served more directly by the stoma-escalation case.
suggestions: Build an application around recurrent bleeding after a documented initial endoscopic course, with hemodynamics, actual target access and prior modalities sufficient to distinguish repeat endoscopy from interventional or operative referral.
Have Melissa verify the exact escalation boundary. Do not manufacture lesion-specific contraindications or choose between equally accepted modalities without deciding information.

title: Endoscopic hemostasis modality selection for peptic-ulcer bleeding

cues.phrase: Epinephrine injection stops the oozing

The comparative role of a particular hemostatic powder and the thermal safety of this exact target need clinician verification; the generic powder label is not evidence that every topical agent has the same role.

The decision mainly recalls injection-plus-another-modality, rather than resolving a difficult rescue question. REJECT_BASIC: the justification acknowledges simplicity but establishes no introductory role.
